pages.title: What this unit is about
pages.body:
> 📝 **Strand 2 — Productivity Software**
Sub-strand 2: Introduction to Presentation Software

Presentation software turns ideas into colourful slides that can be shown on a screen or projector. In this unit you will explore Microsoft PowerPoint, use themes, special characters and proofing tools, format text, and use the Slide Master to give a whole presentation a consistent look. You will design and present your own slide shows.

pages.title: Content standard and lessons
pages.body:
> 🎯 **Content standard**
- **B7.2.2.1** Demonstrate how to use Microsoft PowerPoint (Editing): Introduction to PowerPoint.
- **B7.2.2.2** Demonstrate how to use Microsoft PowerPoint (Formatting).

> 🧭 **What you will be able to do**
- **B7.2.2.1.1** Explain the importance of presentation software.
- **B7.2.2.1.2** Explore features of the MS-PowerPoint interface.
- **B7.2.2.1.3** Demonstrate how to use special characters; design a 7-slide presentation using tools under the Insert ribbon.
- **B7.2.2.2.1** Demonstrate how to change text case, text size, text colour and decorate text.
- **B7.2.2.2.2** Demonstrate how to align text, indent paragraphs, borders and shades.
- **B7.2.2.2.3** Demonstrate the use of the Slide Master and design templates; give a 5-slide presentation.

> 🗺️ **Lessons in this unit**
- 5.1 The Importance of Presentation Software
- 5.2 Exploring the PowerPoint Interface
- 5.3 Special Characters and Building a 7-Slide Presentation
- 5.4 Formatting Text in PowerPoint
- 5.5 Aligning, Indenting, Borders and Shading in PowerPoint
- 5.6 Slide Master and Design Templates

**Core competencies developed:** Digital Literacy (DL5.1), Creativity and Innovation (CI5.4), Communication and Collaboration (CC9.6).

pages.title: The Importance of Presentation Software
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain the meaning of presentation software;
- discuss the benefits of presentation software;
- name common presentation packages.
**Presentation software** is application software used to create a sequence of **slides** containing text, pictures, charts, audio, video and animation, which are displayed to an audience, usually through a projector or large screen. A collection of slides is called a **presentation** or **slide deck**.
## Benefits of presentation software
- Presents information **visually**, making it easier to understand and remember.
- Keeps the speaker **organised** with clear points in a logical order.
- Combines **multimedia**: images, diagrams, charts, sound and video.
- Slides are **easy to edit**, reuse, print as handouts, share or publish online.
- **Speaker notes** remind the presenter what to say.
- Engages the audience through transitions, animations and interactive links.
## Common presentation packages
| **Software** | **Notes** |
|---|---|
| Microsoft PowerPoint | Part of Microsoft 365; the most widely used; saves as .pptx |
| Google Slides | Free, browser-based, real-time collaboration |
| Apple Keynote | Free on Mac, iPhone and iPad |
| LibreOffice Impress | Free and open-source |
| Canva | Online design tool with many presentation templates |
| Corel Presentations | Part of Corel WordPerfect Office |
| Adobe Persuasion | An early presentation program (1988–1997); no longer produced, but important in the history of presentation software |

pages.title: Exploring the PowerPoint Interface
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- identify the parts of the PowerPoint window;
- apply themes and templates;
- use the Proofing and Language tools in PowerPoint.
[[fig:c7-f14|Figure 13: The Microsoft PowerPoint window]]
| **Part** | **Purpose** |
|---|---|
| Slide thumbnails pane | Shows small pictures of all slides; used to select, reorder, duplicate and delete slides |
| Slide pane | The large editing area where you work on the current slide |
| Placeholders | Dotted boxes that hold titles, text, pictures or charts ("Click to add title") |
| Notes pane | Where you type speaker notes; the audience does not see them |
| Ribbon tabs | Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Review, View |
| View buttons | Normal, Slide Sorter, Reading View and Slide Show (F5 starts from the beginning) |
## Themes and templates
A **theme** is a ready-made set of colours, fonts, effects and backgrounds that gives every slide a matching design. A **template** is a ready-made presentation (a .potx file) that may also contain sample slides and content.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Applying a theme**
1. Click the **Design** tab.
2. Point at the themes in the **Themes** group to preview them; click one to apply it to all slides.
3. Choose a colour scheme from the **Variants** group.
4. To start from a template instead, click **File › New** and choose a template, or search online templates (e.g. “education”).

pages.title: Proofing and language tools in PowerPoint
pages.body:
## Proofing and language tools in PowerPoint
As in Word, the **Review** tab contains **Spelling** (F7), **Thesaurus** (Shift + F7), **Translate** and **Language** (set proofing language). Spelling mistakes are underlined in red as you type. Always check spelling before presenting, because errors on a big screen are very visible.

pages.title: Special Characters and Building a 7-Slide Presentation
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- insert special characters and symbols;
- use tools on the Insert ribbon;
- design and present a 7-slide presentation.
## Inserting special characters
**Special characters** are symbols that are not on the keyboard, such as ©, ®, ™, °, ½, €, £, the Ghana cedi sign ₵, Greek letters (π, Ω) and arrows.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Inserting a symbol**
1. Click inside a text box where the symbol should go.
2. Click **Insert › Symbols › Symbol**.
3. Choose a font (e.g. **Calibri** or **Segoe UI Symbol**) and a **Subset** such as **Currency Symbols**.
4. Click the symbol (e.g. **₵**) and click **Insert**, then **Close**.
> ✨ **Did you know?** You can type some symbols directly: hold **Alt** and type **0169** on the numeric keypad for ©, **0176** for °, **0189** for ½. In Word and PowerPoint you can also type the code 20B5 and immediately press **Alt + X** to get the cedi sign ₵.
## Tools on the Insert ribbon
| **Group / tool** | **Use** |
|---|---|
| New Slide | Add a slide with a chosen layout (also on the Home tab) |
| Table | Insert rows and columns of data |
| Pictures, Icons, 3D Models | Add images from the computer, stock images or online sources |
| Shapes, SmartArt, Chart | Draw diagrams and graphs |
| Text Box, WordArt | Add free text and decorative text |
| Header & Footer | Add slide numbers, date and footer text |
| Symbol, Equation | Insert special characters and mathematical equations |
| Video, Audio | Add multimedia |

pages.title: Special Characters and Building a 7-Slide Presentation (continued)
pages.body:
> 💻 **Practical session — Design a 7-slide presentation: “ICT in My Community”**
1. **Slide 1 – Title slide:** title, your name, class and school.
2. **Slide 2 – Introduction:** what ICT means (use bullets).
3. **Slide 3 – ICT tools at home:** insert a picture or icons.
4. **Slide 4 – ICT in school:** insert a table of tools and their uses.
5. **Slide 5 – ICT in business:** use a SmartArt graphic (e.g. Mobile Money, online shops); include the ₵ symbol.
6. **Slide 6 – Dangers and safety:** insert a shape with a warning message.
7. **Slide 7 – Conclusion and thank you:** add a footer with slide numbers on all slides.
8. Apply a theme, check spelling and present your slides to the class using **Slide Show › From Beginning (F5)**.

pages.title: Formatting Text in PowerPoint
pages.body:
Curriculum indicator B7.2.2.2.1
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- use the Font group on the Home ribbon;
- change case, size and colour, and decorate text on slides.
The **Home › Font** group in PowerPoint works like the one in Word: font, size, **Increase/Decrease Font Size**, **Change Case** (Aa), **Bold, Italic, Underline, Text Shadow, Strikethrough**, **Character Spacing**, **Font Colour** and **Clear All Formatting**. Select the text or the whole text box first.
| **Good practice for slide text** | **Why** |
|---|---|
| Titles 32–44 pt; body text at least 24 pt | Text must be readable from the back of the room |
| Use no more than two fonts | Too many fonts look untidy |
| Use contrasting colours (dark text on light background or the reverse) | Low contrast is hard to read, especially on projectors |
| Follow the **6 × 6 rule**: about 6 bullets per slide, 6 words per bullet | Slides support the speaker; they are not a script |
| Avoid long passages in UPPERCASE | Capitals are harder to read and look like shouting |
> 💻 **Practical session**
Open your 7-slide presentation. Change the titles to Capitalize Each Word, increase the title size to 40 pt, apply a theme colour to key words, and add a text shadow to the title on Slide 1.

pages.title: Aligning, Indenting, Borders and Shading in PowerPoint
pages.body:
Curriculum indicators B7.2.2.2.2, B7.2.2.1.2
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- align and indent text on slides;
- add borders (outlines) and shading (fill) to text boxes;
- use the proofing and language tools.
- **Alignment:** Home › Paragraph › Align Left, Centre, Align Right, Justify (Ctrl + L/E/R/J). **Align Text** sets vertical position (top, middle, bottom) in the box.
- **Indenting / list levels:** use **Increase List Level** and **Decrease List Level** (or **Tab** and **Shift + Tab**) to create sub-points. Drag the indent markers on the ruler (View › Ruler) for fine control.
- **Line spacing** and **Columns** are also in the Paragraph group.
- **Borders:** select the text box, then **Shape Format › Shape Outline** (or Home › Drawing › Shape Outline) to choose colour, weight and dash style.
- **Shading:** **Shape Format › Shape Fill** to colour the background of a text box; **Shape Styles** apply ready-made combinations.
> 🧪 **Activity — Review the slides**
Swap presentations with a partner. Use **Review › Spelling**, the **Thesaurus** and **Translate** to check and improve your partner’s slides, then return them with two suggestions for better alignment or shading.

pages.title: Slide Master and Design Templates
pages.body:
Curriculum indicators B7.2.2.2.3, B7.2.2.1.3
> 🎯 **Learning objectives** By the end of this lesson you should be able to:
- explain the purpose of the Slide Master;
- edit the Slide Master;
- save a design template; prepare and give a 5-slide presentation.
The **Slide Master** is the top slide in a hierarchy that stores the design for the whole presentation: background, fonts, colours, placeholder positions, logos and footers. Any change made on the Slide Master appears on **every** slide that uses it. This saves time and keeps the presentation consistent.
> 🪜 **Step by step — Using the Slide Master**
1. Click **View › Master Views › Slide Master**. The large slide at the top of the left pane is the **Slide Master**; the smaller slides below it are **layouts**.
2. Click the Slide Master. Change the title font and colour, and insert your school logo (**Insert › Pictures**) in a corner.
3. Click **Insert › Header & Footer**, tick **Slide number** and **Footer**, type your school name, and click **Apply to All**.
4. Click **Close Master View** (Slide Master tab). Every slide now shows the logo, footer and new fonts.
5. To reuse the design, click **File › Save As**, choose ∗PowerPoint Template (.potx)∗∗ and give it a name such as School_Template.
> 💻 **Practical session — Give a 5-slide presentation**
Using a Slide Master with your school name and logo, prepare a 5-slide presentation on **“Health and Safety in the Computer Lab”**. Use correct text formatting, alignment and a border on one key text box. Present it to the class in two to three minutes.

pages.title: Review: written and practical tasks
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Review exercises** — answer these in your exercise book or on the computer, then check with your teacher.
## Short answer questions
1. State **four** benefits of presentation software.
2. Name the parts of the PowerPoint window and their functions.
3. Explain the difference between a theme and a template.
4. Why should you use the Slide Master instead of formatting each slide separately?
5. State **three** rules for making slide text readable.
## Practical tasks
1. Create a template with a Slide Master showing your school logo and name, and use it for any presentation you make this term.
